01 · The list

Colors,
level by level

The color words of Japanese, from the basic red, blue, white and black to the rarer shades that appear higher up the JLPT lists, each with its reading and meaning.

In Lock&Learn Japanese these words sit in their level packs (JLPT N5, JLPT N3, JLPT N2, JLPT N1), one per glance on the widget: a word waits in kanji, the way the test shows it; one tap reveals the reading, the meaning and a real sentence. JLPT N5 is free; every other pack opens with a free preview and another word unlocks daily.

Type to filter by word, reading or meaning. Flashcards hides the reading and the meaning until you tap a row; Shuffle deals the list in a new order.

03 · Questions

Asked and
answered

What are the basic colors in Japanese?

The table lists every color word on the JLPT vocabulary lists, 26 in all, beginner colors first. Each shows the word, its reading and its English meaning, and the beginner-level words come with a real sentence.

Which JLPT levels are these words from?

13 from JLPT N5, 1 from JLPT N3, 9 from JLPT N2, 3 from JLPT N1. The level chip on each row says where the word sits, so you can stop at your level or read ahead. Beginner-level words carry a real example sentence; the rest show word, reading and meaning, with their sentences in the app.

How do I learn colors words on my iPhone Lock Screen?

Install Lock&Learn Japanese, then touch and hold your Lock Screen, tap Customize, tap the widget area and choose Lock&Learn Japanese. Enable the level packs these words come from (JLPT N5, JLPT N3, JLPT N2 and more). A word waits in kanji, the way the test shows it; one tap reveals the reading, the meaning and a real sentence.

Is Lock&Learn Japanese free?

Yes. The app is free on iOS: JLPT N5 is free, every other pack opens with a free preview, and another word unlocks daily. Lock&Learn+ is an optional upgrade that opens every pack at once, offered as a yearly plan or a one-time lifetime purchase.
